kb_spans.text: MiFID/equivalent business and IBIPs involving investment advice or portfolio management to a **retail client**. S&S ISA + GIA holding MiFID financial instruments → this chapter is the **primary** authority for v1.
kb_spans.title: Applies to (scope)

kb_spans.text:
- On giving investment advice to a retail client, the firm must, **before the transaction concludes**, give a suitability report in a durable medium that states the advice given and how it fits the client's preferences, objectives and other characteristics. [Note: art 25(6) MiFID]
- MiFID Org Reg art 54(12): the report must outline the advice and why the recommendation is suitable — referencing investment term, the client's knowledge & experience, attitude to risk and **capacity for loss** — and flag whether the recommendation will likely need periodic review.
- Distance-communication carve-out: report may follow immediately after conclusion if the client consented to delayed receipt **and** was offered the option to delay the transaction to receive it first.
kb_spans.title: What the report must contain / do (paraphrase)

kb_spans.text: Suitability assessment for MiFID/IBIP investment advice or portfolio management to retail clients. Governs the **client-information substrate** the report must evidence.
kb_spans.title: Applies to (scope)

kb_spans.text:
- Obtain the information needed on the client's (a) **knowledge & experience** in the relevant field, (b) **financial situation including ability to bear losses**, (c) **investment objectives including risk tolerance** — so as to recommend only what is suitable, in particular consistent with the client's risk tolerance and ability to bear losses. [Note: art 25(2) MiFID]
- Financial-situation information must, where relevant, cover source and extent of regular income, assets (including liquid assets, investments, real property) and regular financial commitments.
- Suitability must be assessed for **all decisions to trade — including hold and sell — not only buy** recommendations.
- A bundled package recommended under COBS 6.1ZA.16R must be suitable **as a whole**.
- For a legal person / group of natural persons: establish, record and implement a policy on who is assessed and how, including from whom the information is collected.
kb_spans.title: What the firm must do (paraphrase)

kb_spans.text: Communications and financial promotions to clients. Applies whether the client is retail or professional, taking account of the nature of the client.
kb_spans.title: Applies to (scope)

kb_spans.text: - Ensure a communication or financial promotion is **fair, clear and not misleading**.
kb_spans.title: What the firm must do (paraphrase)

kb_spans.text: All retail-market business with retail customers. In force 31/07/2023 (open products) / 31/07/2024 (closed). For investments, applies to clients who are **not professional clients**. Replaces Principles 6 & 7 where it applies; higher/more exacting standard (PRIN 2A.1.17G).
kb_spans.title: Applies to (scope)

kb_spans.text:
- **Principle 12:** act to deliver good outcomes for retail customers.
- **Cross-cutting rules (PRIN 2A.2):** (i) act in good faith (PRIN 2A.2.1R); (ii) avoid causing foreseeable harm (PRIN 2A.2.8R); (iii) enable and support retail customers to pursue their financial objectives (PRIN 2A.2.14)
- **Four outcomes:** products & services governance (PRIN 2A.3); **price & value / fair value** (PRIN 2A.4); **consumer understanding** (PRIN 2A.5); consumer support (PRIN 2A.6).
- Underpinned by an objective **reasonableness** test, proportionate to the firm's size and role.
kb_spans.title: What the firm must do (paraphrase)

kb_spans.text:
- **PRIN 2A.2.3:** Example of not acting in good faith: 
Failing to take account of client's interests while designing a product or presenting information to them
kb_spans.title: What the firm must avoid (paraphrase)

kb_spans.text: Guidance on how firms comply with Principle 12 + PRIN 2A. Non-binding; does not replace the Handbook (¶1.11). For investments, the Duty applies to **non-professional clients** per COBS (¶2.3).
kb_spans.title: Applies to (scope)

kb_spans.text:
- Duty components: Consumer Principle + three cross-cutting rules + four outcomes (products & services; price & value; consumer understanding; consumer support) (¶1.3).
- **Reasonableness** is an objective test — the standard of a prudent firm carrying on the same activity with understanding of the target market (¶1.4).
- "must / should / may" convention defined (¶1.15).
- Chapter map: Ch.7 = price & value; **Ch.8 = consumer understanding** (communications that equip customers to make effective, timely, informed decisions); Ch.9 = consumer support.
kb_spans.title: What it requires / explains (paraphrase)

kb_spans.text: Overarching conduct standard. Applies to designated investment business for retail clients; MiFID/etc. for any client; insurance distribution for any client. [Note: art 24(1) MiFID]
kb_spans.title: Applies to (scope)

kb_spans.text:
- Act honestly, fairly and professionally in line with the best interests of the client (the **client's best interests rule**).
- This obligation is treated as **including** the duties under Principles 1 (integrity), 2 (skill, care & diligence) and 6 (customers' interests).
kb_spans.title: What the firm must do (paraphrase)

transcript_spans.speaker: ADVISER
transcript_spans.text: Thanks for coming in. To start, what are you hoping to achieve with this money?

transcript_spans.speaker: CLIENT
transcript_spans.text: Mainly to general wealth accumulation. I've got about £39,500 to put in.

transcript_spans.speaker: ADVISER
transcript_spans.text: And what sort of timeframe are you working to?

transcript_spans.speaker: ADVISER
transcript_spans.text: How would you feel if the value fell noticeably in a bad year?

transcript_spans.speaker: CLIENT
transcript_spans.text: I'm happy to take significant risk for higher returns.

transcript_spans.speaker: ADVISER
transcript_spans.text: If you did lose some of this money, how would it affect your day-to-day finances?

transcript_spans.speaker: CLIENT
transcript_spans.text: My take is: substantial liquid assets and high disposable income relative to commitments.

transcript_spans.speaker: ADVISER
transcript_spans.text: Have you invested before, or mostly cash savings?

transcript_spans.speaker: ADVISER
transcript_spans.text: Income and outgoings — roughly £140,700 a year and £3,450 essential monthly costs, is that right?

transcript_spans.speaker: ADVISER
transcript_spans.text: Thanks. I'll review this and set out my recommendation in writing before anything proceeds.
